question: How many essential controls should I prepare for a flow cytometry sorting experiment using Streptavidin beads with five channels, assuming the detection channels are AF350, GFP, PE, AF647, and AF750?

4.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: Minimum for a correct compensation and a negative gate is 1 unstained / beads-only control + 1 single-color compensation control per detection channel.

With AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750 that is

* 1 x unstained beads / unstained cells for autofluorescence / background and for setting the negative population
* 5 x single-stain Streptavidin-bead compensation controls, one for each fluorophore AF350, GFP, PE, AF647, AF750

= 6 controls that are absolutely essential to run the cytometer and sort.

That is the compensation minimum that can be done on streptavidin-fluorophore beads. For a sorting experiment rigorous gate placement you would in practice add the fluorescence-minus-one controls for the panel, 5 FMO controls, one for each channel, giving 1 unstained + 5 single-stains + 5 FMOs = 11 controls for a well controlled sort. The 6 control set is the essential compensation + negative set.

2.text:
For a bead based compensation set up the bead is the matrix and the
fluorochrome is the variable.

Minimum bead based compensation / gating set

* 1 x unstained Streptavidin bead control
  The autofluorescence / scatter baseline of the bead matrix and the
  non specific binding of the biotinylated reagent to the streptavidin
  surface. This is the negative control for all channels and is used for
  threshold and for background subtraction.

* 1 x single colour compensation bead per reporter
  With a 5 colour panel you need one bead population that is saturated
  with a biotinylated antibody / reagent conjugated to only one of the
  five reporters in order to define the spectral spill over of that
  reporter into the other 4 detectors and to set the compensation matrix.

  AF350 , GFP , PE , AF647 , AF750  = 5 single stain compensation tubes

That is 1 + 5 = 6 bead tubes that are strictly required to run the
instrument, build a compensation matrix and set a negative gate.

In practice a sort is set with gating controls as well as compensation
controls. For robust sort gate placement the standard addition is a
Fluorescence Minus One control for each channel, i.e. a bead / cell
staining with the full 5-plex panel minus the fluorochrome of interest.
That allows you to position the positive gate for each channel in the
presence of the spill over from the other 4 fluorochromes.

1 unstained + 5 single stain + 5 FMO = 11 tubes

The 6 tube set is the absolute minimum you can acquire a compensated
data set with. The 11 tube set is the routine best practice for a five
colour sort where sort purity is required. If you are only asked for the
compensation essential set it is the 5 single colour Streptavidin bead
compensation controls plus the unstained Streptavidin bead control.

6.text:
For a bead based compensation the only thing that is absolutely non
negotiable is a compensation standard for each fluorochrome that you will
put on the instrument and an autofluorescence / background reference for
the bead lot.

Streptavidin capture beads are used so that a biotinylated antibody
conjugated to the fluorochrome of interest can be captured on the bead
and gives a bright, uniform single colour emission in the same way as a
cell would.  For n fluorochromes you need n single colour bead
standards and one negative/bead only standard.

* 1 x Streptavidin bead only / unstained bead control - bead
autofluorescence and instrument background
* 1 x AF350 – biotinylated AF350 conjugate on streptavidin beads
* 1 x GFP – biotinylated GFP conjugate on streptavidin beads
* 1 x PE  – biotinylated PE conjugate on streptavidin beads
* 1 x AF647 – biotinylated AF647 conjugate on streptavidin beads
* 1 x AF750 – biotinylated AF750 conjugate on streptavidin beads

That is n + 1 = 5 + 1 = 6 bead controls that will let you build an
accurate n x n compensation matrix for the five detectors AF350, GFP,
PE, AF647 and AF750. In practice the bead compensation is only half of
a sorting experiment.

For robust gate setting on cells you will then normally run on cells

* 1 x fully unstained / viability only cell control for autofluorescence
and for setting the negative population
* 5 x Fluorescence Minus One cell controls, FMO AF350, FMO GFP, FMO PE,
FMO AF647 and FMO AF750, so that the spill-over defined by the bead
compensation can be translated into a biological gate.

With the usual cell based controls that is 1 unstained cell + 5 single
colour compensation beads + 5 FMO cell controls = 11 experimental
controls that are routinely quoted as the minimum best practice for a
5 colour sort, 6 of which are the essential bead-based compensation
controls. Isotype / negative staining controls can be added as needed
for the specific biology.

9.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: Minimum for a valid compensation matrix with streptavidin compensation beads is n+1 bead controls.

For 5 fluorochromes you need one single-color compensation control per fluorochrome and one unstained bead control to set voltage and autofluorescence:

* Unstained streptavidin compensation beads – bead autofluorescence / scatter baseline
* AF350-biotin + streptavidin beads
* GFP-biotin + streptavidin beads
* PE-biotin + streptavidin beads
* AF647-biotin + streptavidin beads
* AF750-biotin + streptavidin beads

That is 5 single-stain + 1 unstained = 6 bead tubes for compensation. The 6 tubes are sufficient to build a 5 × 5 compensation matrix for the AF350 / GFP / PE / AF647 / AF750 detection channels and to set bead voltages.

In practice a sorting experiment is not run on beads alone. Cell autofluorescence and gating need to be validated on the sample matrix. The conventional complete sorting set on top of the 6 bead controls is

* Unstained cells for autofluorescence / voltage setting
* 5 Fluorescence Minus One cell controls, one per channel, to set positive/negative sort gates

That is 1 unstained cells + 5 FMOs = 6 cell controls, i.e. 11 controls in total together with the 6 bead compensation controls, 6 being the absolute minimum compensation requirement.

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: 10

For a 5-color sort on streptavidin beads the minimal practical set I would run is:

* 1 unstained / streptavidin-bead-only control to set baseline autofluorescence and bead scatter
* 5 single-stain compensation controls, one per reporter on streptavidin beads: AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750. These are needed for accurate spectral unmixing/compensation with the bead capture system
* 4 independent fluorescence-minus-one controls for gating. FMOs are used to define positive boundaries in the presence of spillover from the other 4 fluorophores. The AF750 FMO is essentially redundant with the unstained bead control in this panel because AF750 is the far-red dump channel with negligible spillover into the other four detectors, so the unstained bead control already defines the AF750-negative boundary

1 + 5 + 4 = 10 essential controls for setup, compensation and sort gate placement. If a fully conservative FMO for every channel is desired you can add the AF750 FMO as an 11th, but for routine sorting the 10-control set is sufficient and is the one most labs use with streptavidin bead compensation.

11.text:
For a spectrally compensated, sort-ready panel the non-negotiable part of the panel is a negative/blank and a compensation reference for every reporter that will be measured in the list mode file.

With streptavidin capture you can make the compensation references on beads so that the same scatter/bead population is used for all five fluorochromes.

* 1 x Negative / blank
  Unstained cells and/or unstained streptavidin beads alone. This sets autofluorescence/ bead background and the negative gate for all five detectors AF350, GFP/ FITC, PE, AF647 and AF750.

* 5 x Single-stain compensation controls
  One bright, single-colour reference per detector, made on the same streptavidin bead platform that will be used in the experiment, e.g.
  - Streptavidin-beads + biotin- AF350
  - Streptavidin-beads + biotin- GFP
  - Streptavidin-beads + biotin- PE
  - Streptavidin-beads + biotin- AF647
  - Streptavidin-beads + biotin- AF750
  These five are the spectral signatures that are used to build the 5x5 spillover matrix.

That is the absolute minimum, 1 + 5 = 6 independent control tubes/samples, that are required to be able to set voltages, perform compensation and define a negative population for a 5-colour sort.

In practice a sort is almost always run with fluorescence-minus-one controls to set the positive gates in the presence of spillover, i.e. 5 x FMOs:

FMO AF350, FMO GFP, FMO PE, FMO AF647, FMO AF750,
each containing all 5 biotinylated reagents except the one that is omitted.

With the FMOs the widely used best-practice set is

1 unstained/ beads-only + 5 single-stain compensation + 5 FMO = 11 tubes,
plus a viability dye control if a live/dead discriminator is in the panel. The 6 tube unstained + single-stain set is the essential minimum for compensation and a negative gate; the 5 FMOs are the additional controls that are routinely considered essential for accurate gating in a multi-colour sort.

12.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: 10

For a 5-color sort with AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750 on streptavidin beads the sorting gates have to be set on compensation-corrected data and on background fluorescence, so the minimal practical set is the compensation set plus the gate-setting set.

Compensation: one single-stain streptavidin bead control per fluorochrome for spectral unmixing
* AF350 single
* GFP single
* PE single
* AF647 single
* AF750 single
= 5 controls

Gate setting for sorting: Fluorescence Minus One controls are essential to define positive vs negative boundaries when multiple parameters are used together, especially with a bead-based reporter where autofluorescence can shift.
* FMO minus AF350
* FMO minus GFP
* FMO minus PE
* FMO minus AF647
* FMO minus AF750
= 5 controls

That is 5 + 5 = 10 essential controls. The unstained bead/cell background is effectively represented within the FMO series, so a separate unstained tube is not counted as an additional independent essential control for compensation and sort gate definition in this bead-based panel.

PUBLIC RESPONSE: 10 essential controls.

For a 5-fluorophore streptavidin bead panel you need one single-stain compensation control per fluorophore to build the compensation matrix, and one fluorescence-minus-one control per channel to set sorting gates in the presence of spillover. 

That is 5 single-color streptavidin bead compensation controls: AF350-bead, GFP-bead, PE-bead, AF647-bead and AF750-bead, plus 5 FMO bead controls: FMO-AF350, FMO-GFP, FMO-PE, FMO-AF647 and FMO-AF750. The FMOs provide the effective unstained baseline for gating in a multi-color sort, so the set of 5 + 5 = 10 controls covers compensation and gate placement for all five detection channels.

5.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: 10

For a 5-parameter sort the minimum practical set that lets you both compensate and set accurate sorting gates is one compensation/single-stain control per detection channel and one Fluorescence Minus One control per channel.

Compensation: AF350, GFP, PE, AF647, AF750 on streptavidin beads or equivalent single-stained material = 5 controls. These define the spillover matrix for the 5 channels.

Sorting gates: one FMO per channel is needed to define the boundary for a positive population in the presence of the other four fluorochromes, which is critical for purity when sorting. AF350 FMO, GFP FMO, PE FMO, AF647 FMO, AF750 FMO = 5 controls.

That is 5 + 5 = 10 controls. An unstained bead/cell sample is useful for instrument background but in a bead-based sorting workflow the FMOs already provide the effective negative baseline for each channel and are the controls actually used to position the sort gates, so the core essential set for compensation and gate setting is ten.

3.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: In practice the compensation that must be done on the 5 detector channels is the hard essential requirement and the unstained/autofluorescence reference that defines where the non-fluorescent population sits.

With Streptavidin capture beads the compensation set is made on the beads themselves.
* 1 × beads alone / unstained reference. This is the autofluorescence/background of the Streptavidin bead matrix and it is the negative reference for the instrument and for the AF350 / GFP / PE / AF647 / AF750 detectors.
* 1 × single fluorochrome compensation control per detection channel. On Streptavidin beads this is normally a biotinylated antibody or dye that is captured on the beads and gives a bright positive signal in only one detector at a time.

That is 1 + 5 = 6 bead preparations that are strictly essential for a compensated sort.

1 AF350 single stain beads
1 GFP single stain beads
1 PE single stain beads
1 AF647 single stain beads
1 AF750 single stain beads
1 unstained / beads alone

Those 6 samples give you an unstained reference and a compensation matrix for the 5-colour panel. 

For a sorting experiment where the gating boundaries matter, best practice is to add Fluorescence Minus One controls for each channel to set positive vs negative gates in the presence of spectral spill-over. That is 5 additional FMO bead/cell samples, 5 single stain + 1 unstained + 5 FMO = 11 samples in total for a rigorously gated sort. The 6 compensation + unstained set is the minimal essential set.

8.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: For a 5-colour panel a compensation matrix can be built from a negative/ unstained control plus one single-fluorochrome compensation control per colour. 

With the panel AF350 / GFP / PE / AF647 / AF750 that is

* 1 x unstained / beads-only / negative control for background autofluorescence and to set the negative population and the voltage / threshold for sorting
* 5 x single-stain compensation controls, one for each fluorochrome, on Streptavidin-capture beads.  AF350-bead, GFP-bead, PE-bead, AF647-bead and AF750-bead are used to calculate the spectral overlap matrix for the 5 detection channels.

That is the essential minimum of 1 + 5 = 6 distinct bead / sample controls for compensation and negative gating. 

In practice for a sort you will want robust gate placement as well. Best practice adds a Fluorescence-Minus-One control for each channel to define spill-over for the gating boundaries, i.e. 5 FMO controls, giving the commonly quoted 1 unstained + 5 single-stain + 5 FMO = 11 sample controls for a 5-colour sort. The 5 single-stain + 1 unstained set is the absolute essential compensation / negative set.

2.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The question is about how many essential controls for a 5-channel streptavidin-bead sorting panel AF350, GFP, PE, AF647, AF750.

Core disagreement is what counts as "essential" for a sort vs absolute minimum for compensation.

Minimum compensation set repeatedly cited:
* 1 unstained/beads-only control for autofluorescence/background, voltage/threshold and negative population
* 5 single-stain Streptavidin-bead compensation controls, one per fluorochrome: AF350-bead, GFP-bead, PE-bead, AF647-bead, AF750-bead
=> 1 + 5 = 6 bead tubes. This is the non-negotiable set to build a 5x5 spillover matrix and set a negative gate. Colleagues 10,11,2,3,4,6,8,9 all state this as absolute minimum.

1.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I’m leaning with the 5 + 5 framing that Colleagues 1, 12 and 5 are laying out, because it matches what is actually used to set up and run the sort.

With streptavidin-capture compensation beads the non-negotiable part for the instrument is a single-stain reference per reporter so we can build the 5×5 spillover matrix for AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750. That is 5 bead controls:
* AF350-biotin + streptavidin beads
* GFP-biotin + streptavidin beads
* PE-biotin + streptavidin beads
* AF647-biotin + streptavidin beads
* AF750-biotin + streptavidin beads

For a sort the gates are not set on a naked negative population, they are set in the presence of the other four fluorochromes. That is exactly what the FMO series gives us: one tube with the full 5-plex minus the channel of interest, run on the same bead / sample matrix, so the spillover from the remaining four reporters is present and the negative boundary for that channel is defined in the context it will be sorted.

* FMO minus AF350
* FMO minus GFP
* FMO minus PE
* FMO minus AF647
* FMO minus AF750

= 5 gating controls.

The unstained / beads-only tube is useful for initial voltage/threshold setting and for checking bead autofluorescence, but operationally that negative baseline is already sampled inside each FMO: each FMO is the panel background for the omitted channel while the other four fluorochromes are on. Counting an additional separate unstained beads-only tube as an independent essential control for compensation and sort gate definition is double counting the same negative information that the FMOs already provide.

So for compensation plus the gate placement that actually drives sort purity we are at 5 single-stain compensation beads + 5 FMOs = 10 essential controls for a 5-channel streptavidin bead sort. An extra unstained cell/bead tube is good practice for documentation and for voltage set-up, but it isn’t a distinct essential control beyond what the FMO series already supplies for gating.

5.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: For a sort-ready 5-colour streptavidin bead panel the controls that actually drive the experiment are the ones you need to build the compensation matrix and to place positive gates in the presence of spillover.

Compensation with streptavidin capture:
* AF350 single-stain streptavidin bead
* GFP single-stain streptavidin bead
* PE single-stain streptavidin bead
* AF647 single-stain streptavidin bead
* AF750 single-stain streptavidin bead

Those five define the 5x5 spillover signatures for AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750. That is the non-negotiable compensation set.

Gate setting for sorting:
A sort gate must be placed on compensated data in the context of the other four fluorochromes. FMOs give you that context.
* FMO minus AF350
* FMO minus GFP
* FMO minus PE
* FMO minus AF647
* FMO minus AF750

Each FMO contains the full bead/cell staining cocktail minus one reporter, so it shows the exact spread of the remaining four fluorochromes into the detector of interest plus the bead/autofluorescence background. That is the effective negative for each channel in the real staining condition.

The beads-only/unstained bead control is useful for initial voltage and background check, but in a bead-based compensation workflow its information is already contained within the FMO series. Every FMO includes the bead matrix and the full spillover background; the unstained bead population is a subset of the negative tail seen in each FMO. Counting a separate unstained tube on top of the five FMOs is double counting the background for sort gate definition.

So the practical, essential set for compensation and for defining sorting gates is 5 single-stain bead compensation controls + 5 FMO controls = 10 essential controls. The 6-tube 1 unstained + 5 single-stain minimum is correct for compensation alone, but for a sorting experiment the FMOs replace the standalone unstained as the working negative for gate placement, giving 10 controls that cover both matrix generation and robust sort gate setting.

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I think the 11-tube set is the routine best practice people quote for a sorting-ready 5-colour panel, and it's worth being clear what is truly independent and what is double counting.

With streptavidin-capture compensation beads the non-negotiable compensation part is five single-stain bead standards, one per reporter:
AF350-bead, GFP-bead, PE-bead, AF647-bead, AF750-bead.
Those five build the 5x5 spillover matrix for AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750.

For sorting the gates have to be set in the presence of spillover from the other four fluorochromes. That is what the Fluorescence Minus One series does. One FMO per channel is needed to define the positive vs negative boundary for that channel when the other four are on:
FMO minus AF350, FMO minus GFP, FMO minus PE, FMO minus AF647, FMO minus AF750.
That is five controls that actually position the sort gates.

The unstained / beads-only tube is useful for initial voltage and autofluorescence checks, but in a bead-based sorting workflow its information is already embodied in the FMO series. Counting an additional independent unstained control on top of the five FMOs is double counting the same negative baseline.

So the practical essential, independent set for a compensated sort is the compensation set plus the gate-setting set:
5 single-stain streptavidin bead compensation controls + 5 FMO bead/cell controls = 10 essential controls.

The 1 unstained + 5 single-stain = 6 tube absolute compensation minimum is correct for the matrix alone, and 11 tubes is the conservative reporting number if you insist on listing unstained separately from the FMOs.   AF350-biotin + streptavidin beads
  GFP-biotin + streptavidin beads
  PE-biotin + streptavidin beads
  AF647-biotin + streptavidin beads
  AF750-biotin + streptavidin beads

That is the absolute compensation floor, 1 + 5 = 6 bead tubes, that will let you build a 5 × 5 spillover matrix and define a negative population.

A sort is gated much more stringently than an analysis. In practice the 6-tube compensation set is routinely extended with gate-setting controls so the positive boundary for each channel can be placed in the presence of spill-over from the other four fluorochromes:

* 5 x Fluorescence Minus One controls, one per channel, e.g. FMO-AF350, FMO-GFP, FMO-PE, FMO-AF647, FMO-AF750, made on the same sample matrix that will be sorted.

With the conventional cell-based gating set that is

1 unstained / beads-only + 5 single-stain streptavidin bead compensation + 5 FMO = 11 tubes

for a rigorously gated, sort-ready 5-colour panel. The 1 unstained + 5 single-stain = 6 bead controls are the essential minimum for compensation and a negative gate; the 5 FMOs are the additional controls that are routinely considered essential for accurate sort gate placement and purity. If the unstained baseline is taken as already represented within the FMO series the bead-based compensation + gating set is commonly quoted as 5 single-stain + 5 FMO = 10 controls.

For a 5-fluorophore streptavidin bead panel the controls you actually use to run the sorter are the compensation references and the gate-setting references.

Compensation has to be built on the same matrix you will sort with, so with streptavidin capture you need one single-stain bead control per reporter to define spillover:

* Streptavidin beads + biotin-AF350
* Streptavidin beads + biotin-GFP
* Streptavidin beads + biotin-PE
* Streptavidin beads + biotin-AF647
* Streptavidin beads + biotin-AF750

That is 5 single-stain bead controls for the 5 x 5 matrix on AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750.

Sort gate placement is not done against an isolated bead-only autofluorescence population. On a sorter you need the negative boundary for each channel in the presence of the other four fluorochromes. That is exactly what an FMO provides. An FMO for a given channel contains the full 5-plex streptavidin bead staining minus that channel, so it gives you the spillover-defined negative peak for that detector in the experimental staining context.

* FMO minus AF350
* FMO minus GFP
* FMO minus PE
* FMO minus AF647
* FMO minus AF750

5 FMOs.

The bead-only / unstained bead tube is a voltage / background check, but with a bead-based compensation set it is functionally embedded. The negative population for each detector is already present in the FMO series, and the bead autofluorescence component is captured in the single-stain bead set and in the unstained portion of each FMO. In routine sorting practice those 5 single-stain beads + 5 FMOs are the set that is actually used for compensation matrix generation and for positioning positive/negative sort gates. That is 5 + 5 = 10 essential controls for a sorting-ready streptavidin bead 5-color panel.

For a 5 detector panel the compensation matrix is the non-negotiable part of a sort and with streptavidin capture beads the matrix is built on the bead platform itself.

Non-negotiable bead compensation minimum

* 1 x unstained / beads only streptavidin beads. Bead autofluorescence / scatter baseline and the negative reference for voltage and background subtraction for AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750.
* 1 x single-stain streptavidin bead control per fluorochrome for the spill-over matrix
  * Streptavidin beads + biotin-AF350
  * Streptavidin beads + biotin-GFP
  * Streptavidin beads + biotin-PE
  * Streptavidin beads + biotin-AF647
  * Streptavidin beads + biotin-AF750

That is 1 unstained + 5 single-stain = 6 bead tubes that are strictly required to set voltages, generate a valid 5 × 5 spill-over matrix and define a negative population for the five channels. Those 6 are the absolute compensation minimum.

A sort is gated on compensated data and the gates have to be placed in the presence of spill-over. For a sorting-ready, purity driven experiment that compensation minimum is normally extended with gate-setting controls on the sample matrix:

* 1 x unstained cells for sample autofluorescence / viability background
* 5 x Fluorescence Minus One cell controls, FMO AF350, FMO GFP, FMO PE, FMO AF647, FMO AF750, one per channel to position each positive sort gate in the presence of the other four fluorochromes

With the conventional cell-based gating set added to the bead compensation set this is the widely quoted sorting-ready essential set:

1 unstained cells + 5 single-stain streptavidin beads + 5 FMO cells = 11 tubes

The 1 + 5 = 6 bead controls remain the essential compensation / negative minimum. The 5 FMOs are the additional controls that are routinely considered essential for accurate gate placement and sort purity in a 5-colour sort. If the unstained cell control is counted as already covered by the FMO series, the bead-compensation + FMO core is 5 single-stain + 5 FMO = 10 controls.

1.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I’m finding the operational “what do we actually use to set the matrix and draw the sort gates” framing helpful, because that’s what ends up driving purity on the sorter.

With streptavidin capture the compensation matrix has to be built on the bead matrix. That means one single-stain bead reference per reporter for AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750. That is 5 bead controls that are non-negotiable for a 5×5 spillover matrix.

For the sort itself the decision is made on compensated data with gates placed in the presence of spillover from the other four fluorochromes. An FMO gives exactly that context: the full 5-plex staining minus the channel of interest, on the same bead / sample matrix, so the negative boundary for the omitted channel is seen with the other four fluorochromes on and with spillover compensated.

* FMO minus AF350
* FMO minus GFP
* FMO minus PE
* FMO minus AF647
* FMO minus AF750

That is 5 gating controls that are used to position each positive/negative sort boundary under the experimental staining conditions.

The beads-only / unstained bead tube is useful for an initial voltage/threshold check and for documenting bead autofluorescence. Operationally though that baseline is already sampled in every FMO. Each FMO contains the bead matrix plus four fluorochromes, so the fluorescence in the omitted detector is bead autofluorescence plus spillover from the four present reporters. That is the effective negative you use for gate placement for that channel. Counting a separate unstained tube on top of the five FMOs repeats the same bead autofluorescence information for gating purposes.

So for compensation matrix generation plus the gate placement that actually drives the sort, the non-redundant set we run and rely on is 5 single-stain streptavidin bead compensation controls + 5 FMOs = 10 controls.

The 1 unstained + 5 single-stain = 6 bead minimum is correct for building a matrix, and listing unstained separately to get to 11 is a conservative documentation practice. If the question is about the essential, non-redundant controls that are actually used to define the compensation matrix and to set sort gates in the presence of spillover, the core is the 5+5 = 10 set.

3.text:
For a 5-colour streptavidin-capture sort the controls that are actually used to run the sorter are the compensation references and the gate-setting references, not an isolated bead-only negative.

Compensation has to be built on the same matrix you will sort with. That is non-negotiable on beads:
* Streptavidin beads + biotin-AF350
* Streptavidin beads + biotin-GFP
* Streptavidin beads + biotin-PE
* Streptavidin beads + biotin-AF647
* Streptavidin beads + biotin-AF750

5 single-stain bead controls define the 5×5 spillover matrix for AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750.

Sort gate placement is not done against an isolated autofluorescence population. On a sorter you need the negative boundary for each channel in the presence of the other four fluorochromes. That is exactly what an FMO provides on the sample/bead staining matrix:
* FMO minus AF350
* FMO minus GFP
* FMO minus PE
* FMO minus AF647
* FMO minus AF750

5 FMOs.

The beads-only / unstained streptavidin bead tube is useful for initial voltage/threshold and for checking bead autofluorescence, and it is the n+1 = 1 unstained + 5 single-stain = 6 tube absolute compensation floor. Operationally that negative baseline is already sampled inside each FMO: each FMO is the panel background for the omitted channel while the other four reporters are present, and the bead autofluorescence component is captured in the single-stain bead set and in the negative tail of the FMOs. Counting an additional independent unstained beads-only tube on top of the five FMOs for sort gate definition is double counting.

Hence the practical, non-redundant essential set for compensation matrix generation and for positioning positive/negative sort gates is

5 single-stain streptavidin bead compensation controls + 5 FMO controls = 10 essential controls

for a sorting-ready streptavidin bead 5-colour panel.

That is the 6-tube 1 unstained + 5 single-stain absolute compensation minimum extended to a sort-ready set. If unstained/beads-only is insisted on as a separately listed control in addition to the FMOs the conservative reporting number is 1 unstained + 5 singles + 5 FMOs = 11 tubes, with the 6 tube set being the non-negotiable compensation + negative floor.

5.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I’ve been following the bead vs cell matrix discussion and I think the practical, non-redundant set for a sorting-ready 5-channel streptavidin panel is the 5 single-stain compensation beads + 5 FMOs = 10 essential controls.

Compensation on this platform has to be built on the same streptavidin matrix you will sort with. That is non-negotiable:
* Streptavidin beads + biotin-AF350
* Streptavidin beads + biotin-GFP
* Streptavidin beads + biotin-PE
* Streptavidin beads + biotin-AF647
* Streptavidin beads + biotin-AF750

Those five define the 5×5 spillover matrix for AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750. That is the instrument minimum.

Sort gate placement is different from analysis. On a sorter you do not gate a channel against an isolated autofluorescence population, you place the positive/negative boundary in the presence of spillover from the other four reporters. That is exactly the FMO:
* FMO minus AF350
* FMO minus GFP
* FMO minus PE
* FMO minus AF647
* FMO minus AF750

Each FMO is the full 5-plex streptavidin bead staining minus one reporter, so it shows the bead autofluorescence plus the spillover from the remaining four fluorochromes into the omitted detector. That is the operational negative you use for that channel in the actual staining context, and it therefore sets the voltage-threshold and the compensated gate boundary at the same time.

The beads-only / unstained bead tube is useful for initial voltage checks and documentation of bead autofluorescence, but in a bead-based compensation workflow its information is already sampled inside the FMO series. Every FMO contains the bead matrix and the full spillover background; the unstained bead population is a subset of the negative tail seen in each FMO. Counting an additional separate unstained beads-only tube on top of the five FMOs is double counting the same background for gate definition.

That is why Colleague 11 notes “if the unstained cell control is counted as already covered by the FMO series, the bead-compensation + FMO core is 5 single-stain + 5 FMO = 10 controls.” Colleague 2 makes the same point: “if the unstained bead control is taken as the effective negative baseline for the FMO series the routinely quoted practical bead-based number is 5 singles + 5 FMOs = 10 controls.” Colleague 4 likewise says “if the unstained bead baseline is taken as being subsumed in the FMO series, the distinct compensation + gate-setting set is commonly quoted as 5 single-stain + 5 FMO = 10 essential controls.”

So for compensation matrix generation and for positioning positive sort gates in compensated space the independent essential set is 5 single-stain streptavidin bead compensation controls + 5 FMO controls = 10. An extra unstained beads-only tube is good practice for documentation and initial set-up, but it is not an additional essential control beyond what the FMO series already provides for sorting gate placement.

4.text:
For a streptavidin-capture 5-colour sort the instrument requirements split into compensation and gate placement, and on beads they are largely independent.

Compensation is non-negotiable and it is built on the bead matrix:

* Streptavidin beads + biotin-AF350
* Streptavidin beads + biotin-GFP
* Streptavidin beads + biotin-PE
* Streptavidin beads + biotin-AF647
* Streptavidin beads + biotin-AF750

Those 5 single-stain bead standards give the 5×5 spill-over matrix for AF350 / GFP / PE / AF647 / AF750.

Sort gates are not placed on an isolated bead autofluorescence population. They have to be placed in compensated space in the presence of spill-over from the other four reporters. That is the FMO definition:

* FMO minus AF350 : full 5-plex minus AF350
* FMO minus GFP   : full 5-plex minus GFP
* FMO minus PE    : full 5-plex minus PE
* FMO minus AF647 : full 5-plex minus AF647
* FMO minus AF750 : full 5-plex minus AF750

Each FMO is the working negative for its omitted channel in the experimental staining context, i.e. bead autofluorescence + the spread of the remaining four fluorochromes into the detector of interest.

That is 5 single-stain compensation beads + 5 FMO gate-setting controls = 10 independent, operationally essential controls for a compensated, purity-driven sort.

A Streptavidin beads-only / unstained bead tube is useful for initial voltage/threshold setting and for documentation of bead autofluorescence. In practice its negative information is sampled inside the FMO series; each FMO already contains the bead matrix and the background of the four fluorochromes that are present. Counting a separate unstained beads-only tube on top of the five FMOs is double counting the same negative baseline for gate placement.

The conventional conservative reporting is therefore 1 unstained/beads-only + 5 single-stain beads + 5 FMOs = 11 tubes, with the 1+5 = 6 bead tubes being the absolute compensation minimum. The non-redundant essential set that actually drives both matrix generation and robust sort gate placement is the 5+5 = 10 control set described above.

PUBLIC RESPONSE: I agree with Colleagues 10, 11, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8 and 9 that an 11-tube listing is the conservative, sorting-ready best practice that most labs quote for documentation, and that the 1+5 = 6 bead set is the absolute compensation minimum. Where I land on what is essential and non-redundant in practice is the 10-tube set that Colleagues 1, 12, 5 and 7 are articulating.

With a streptavidin-capture matrix the compensation matrix has to be built on beads. The independent references that define the 5x5 spillover for AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750 are:

* Streptavidin beads + biotin-AF350
* Streptavidin beads + biotin-GFP
* Streptavidin beads + biotin-PE

* FMO minus AF350
* FMO minus GFP
* FMO minus PE
* FMO minus AF647
* FMO minus AF750

Each FMO contains the full streptavidin bead staining cocktail minus one reporter, so it shows the bead autofluorescence plus the spillover-defined negative peak for the omitted channel under the exact staining conditions that will be sorted.

The beads-only / unstained bead tube is useful for initial voltage/threshold checks, but operationally its negative baseline is already sampled inside the FMO series. In practice for a bead-compensated sort you need the 5 single-stain bead references to build the matrix and the 5 FMOs to set the gates in context. 11.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: For a sorting experiment the compensation matrix and the gate-setting controls are both essential, and they are not the same thing.

On a streptavidin capture platform the spectral matrix has to be built on the bead matrix:

FMO minus AF350
FMO minus GFP
FMO minus PE
FMO minus AF647
FMO minus AF750

6.text:
For a streptavidin-capture 5-colour sort the instrument requirement and the sorting-purity requirement are different things and both are being conflated here.

Compensation non-negotiable on the bead platform
The 5 x 5 spill-over matrix for AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750 has to be built on the same matrix you will use for compensation.

* 1 x Streptavidin beads only / unstained bead control – bead autofluorescence / scatter baseline, voltage / threshold setting and the negative reference for all five detectors

  Streptavidin beads + biotin-GFP
  Streptavidin beads + biotin-PE
  Streptavidin beads + biotin-AF647
  Streptavidin beads + biotin-AF750

That is 1 + 5 = 6 bead tubes that are strictly required to build a valid compensation matrix and to define a negative population. Those six are the absolute, non-negotiable compensation minimum.

* FMO minus AF350
* FMO minus GFP
* FMO minus PE
* FMO minus AF647
* FMO minus AF750

The 6-tube bead compensation set therefore has to be extended with gate-setting controls for a purity driven sort.

1 unstained/beads-only + 5 single-stain streptavidin bead compensation + 5 FMO = 11 tubes

The 10-control non-redundant reporting, 5 single-stain + 5 FMO, is the practical set that is actually used for matrix generation and gate positioning because each FMO already contains the bead matrix and the spill-over background for the channel that is omitted. It is functionally equivalent to 11 tubes with the beads-only voltage/threshold check being counted inside the FMO series. A 1 × unstained / beads-only streptavidin bead reference for bead autofluorescence / scatter baseline, voltage/threshold and the negative reference for the five detectors is the absolute compensation minimum together with the five single stains:

* FMO minus GFP
* FMO minus PE
* FMO minus AF647
* FMO minus AF750

5 single-stain streptavidin bead compensation controls + 5 FMO gate-setting controls = 10 essential controls

3.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE:

I’m converging on the 5 single-stain bead + 5 FMO operational core as the essential, non-redundant set that actually drives both the matrix and the sort gate for a streptavidin-capture 5-plex.

Compensation on this platform is bead-based and non-negotiable:
* Streptavidin beads + biotin-AF350
* Streptavidin beads + biotin-GFP
* Streptavidin beads + biotin-PE
* Streptavidin beads + biotin-AF647
* Streptavidin beads + biotin-AF750

That is 5 single-stain streptavidin bead compensation controls for the 5 × 5 spillover matrix for AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750.

Sort gate placement on a sorter is in compensated space in the presence of spillover from the other four reporters. That is what an FMO gives on the same staining matrix:
* FMO minus AF350
* FMO minus GFP
* FMO minus PE
* FMO minus AF647
* FMO minus AF750

5 FMO gate-setting controls.

The beads-only / unstained streptavidin tube is useful for initial voltage/threshold and documentation of bead autofluorescence. Operationally that negative baseline is already sampled inside the FMO series: each FMO contains the bead matrix plus four fluorochromes, so the negative peak seen in the omitted detector is bead autofluorescence + spillover from the four present reporters in the exact staining context that will be sorted. Counting a separate unstained beads-only tube on top of the five FMOs therefore double counts the same background for gate definition.

Hence the practical, independent set that is actually used to generate the compensation matrix and to position positive/negative sort boundaries is

5 single-stain streptavidin bead compensation controls + 5 FMO controls = 10 essential, non-redundant controls.

The 1 unstained/beads-only + 5 single-stain = 6 bead tube set remains the absolute compensation + negative minimum, and the conservatively reported sorting-ready listing 1 unstained/beads-only + 5 single-stain + 5 FMO = 11 tubes is the same core with the unstained baseline listed separately for documentation/voltage set up.

Compensation on this platform is bead-based and non-negotiable:
* Streptavidin beads + biotin-AF350
* Streptavidin beads + biotin-GFP
* Streptavidin beads + biotin-PE
* Streptavidin beads + biotin-AF647
* Streptavidin beads + biotin-AF750

Those five define the 5×5 spillover matrix for the five detectors. That part is fixed.

Sort gate placement is what changes the count. A purity-driven sort is gated on compensated data in the presence of spillover from the other four reporters. That is exactly what an FMO gives on the same bead/staining matrix:
* FMO minus AF350
* FMO minus GFP
* FMO minus PE
* FMO minus AF647
* FMO minus AF750

Each FMO is the full 5-plex streptavidin bead staining minus one reporter, so the negative peak seen in the omitted detector is bead autofluorescence plus spillover from the four present reporters in the exact staining context that will be sorted. That is the operational negative used for gate placement for that channel.

The beads-only / unstained streptavidin tube is useful for an initial voltage/threshold check and for documenting bead autofluorescence. Operationally that baseline is already sampled in every FMO. Each FMO contains the bead matrix plus four fluorochromes, so the fluorescence in the omitted detector is the effective negative you use for that channel. On a streptavidin capture platform the compensation matrix must be built on the bead matrix. That is non-negotiable:

* 1 × Streptavidin beads only / unstained bead control – bead autofluorescence / scatter baseline, voltage / threshold setting and the true negative reference for AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750
* 1 × single-stain streptavidin bead compensation control per reporter for the 5 × 5 spill-over matrix
  Streptavidin beads + biotin-AF350
  Streptavidin beads + biotin-GFP
  Streptavidin beads + biotin-PE
  Streptavidin beads + biotin-AF647
  Streptavidin beads + biotin-AF750

That is 1 + 5 = 6 bead tubes, the absolute compensation + negative minimum.

A sort is not an analysis. The positive/negative boundary for each detector has to be placed on compensated data in the presence of spill-over from the other four fluorochromes. That is the FMO definition on the same staining matrix that will be sorted:

* FMO minus AF350
* FMO minus GFP
* FMO minus PE
* FMO minus AF647
* FMO minus AF750

That is 5 gating controls.

Conventional sorting-ready reporting therefore is:

1 beads-only + 5 single-stain streptavidin bead compensation + 5 FMO = 11 tubes

6 of which are the essential compensation / negative minimum and 5 FMOs are the essential gate-setting controls for sort purity.

The 5 single-stain + 5 FMO = 10 non-redundant operational core noted by Colleagues 1,5,7,12 is correct as a book-keeping collapse: each FMO already samples bead autofluorescence plus spill-over from the four present reporters, so the independent information used to build the matrix and to position the gates is functionally 5 + 5. I keep the beads-only tube listed separately for documentation, voltage/threshold set-up and an independent autofluorescence reference, which is why the rigorously gated, reporting-ready essential set for a 5-channel streptavidin bead sort on AF350, GFP, PE, AF647, AF750 is quoted as 11 tubes, with 1+5 = 6 tubes as the absolute compensation minimum.

For a streptavidin capture 5-plex sort the compensation matrix and the sort gate placement are two different requirements and both have to be met on the bead matrix that will be sorted.

Compensation is non-negotiable and bead based for AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750:

* 1 x Streptavidin beads only / unstained bead control - bead autofluorescence/scatter baseline, voltage / threshold setting and the negative reference for all five detectors
* 1 x single-stain streptavidin bead compensation control per reporter for the 5 x 5 spill-over matrix
  Streptavidin beads + biotin-AF350
  Streptavidin beads + biotin-GFP
  Streptavidin beads + biotin-PE
  Streptavidin beads + biotin-AF647
  Streptavidin beads + biotin-AF750

That is 1 unstained + 5 singles = 6 bead tubes. Those 6 are the absolute compensation / negative minimum.

Sort gate placement
Compensation alone does not place a purity driven sort gate. The positive/negative boundary for each detector has to be set in compensated space in the presence of spill-over from the other four fluorochromes. That is what an FMO provides on the same staining matrix that will be sorted:

* FMO minus AF350
* FMO minus GFP
* FMO minus PE
* FMO minus AF647
* FMO minus AF750

= 5 FMO controls.

Conventional sorting-ready reporting therefore is

1 beads-only + 5 single-stain streptavidin bead compensation + 5 FMO = 11 tubes

6 of which are the essential compensation/negative minimum and 5 FMOs are the essential gate-setting controls for sort purity.

Operationally the beads-only negative baseline is functionally embedded in the FMO series. Each FMO contains the bead matrix + four fluorochromes so the negative peak seen in the omitted detector is bead autofluorescence plus spill-over from the four present reporters, i.e. the operational negative used for gating. In that non-redundant working view the independent set that actually drives matrix generation and gate placement is 5 single-stain streptavidin bead compensation controls + 5 FMO controls = 10 essential, non-redundant controls, with the beads-only tube being the additional conservative voltage/background check that brings the routinely quoted set to 11. The 1+5 = 6 bead set remains the absolute compensation minimum.

* FMO minus GFP
* FMO minus PE

The beads-only / unstained streptavidin tube is useful for initial voltage/threshold and for documenting bead autofluorescence. PRIVATE REFLECTION: The 5-detector streptavidin bead panel AF350, GFP, PE, AF647, AF750 has settled consensus on component controls, with only counting semantics remaining.

Core non-negotiable agreement across rounds:
* Compensation matrix is bead-based and requires one single-stain streptavidin bead control per fluorochrome =5 controls: AF350-bead, GFP-bead, PE-bead, AF647-bead, AF750-bead.
* A negative / beads-only / unstained reference is needed for autofluorescence/background, voltage/threshold setting and a negative population.
* Instrument minimum is unanimous: n+1 = 1 unstained/beads-only +5 single-stain beads =6 bead tubes to build a 5x5 spillover matrix and define a negative population. Colleagues 10,11,2,3,4,6,8,9 state this as the non-negotiable minimum.

Sorting gate placement:
* FMOs are now widely argued as essential for a purity-critical sort. The FMO series gives positive/negative boundary for each channel in presence of the other four fluorochromes. 5 FMO controls, one per channel: FMO minus AF350, FMO minus GFP, FMO minus PE, FMO minus AF647, FMO minus AF750.
* Colleagues 1,10,11,12,3,4,5,7,9 now explicitly frame the practical essential independent set as 5 single-stain compensation beads +5 FMOs =10 controls, with unstained/beads-only baseline functionally embedded in the FMO series. Unstained tube is useful for voltage set-up but is double counted if listed separately from FMOs for gate definition.
* Conservative counting still adds explicit unstained/beads-only on top of singles and FMOs: 1 unstained +5 single +5 FMO =11 tubes. Colleagues 2,6,8 give this as routine best-practice sorting-ready set, with 6 being essential compensation minimum and 11 practical sorting set. They distinguish bead controls for compensation and cell controls for gating, often citing 1 unstained cells +5 single-stain beads +5 FMO cells.

Unresolved for me:
Whether “essential” means only compensation+negative minimum =6, or includes FMO gate-setting for a sort =10/11, and whether explicit unstained control remains separate from FMOs in bead-based workflow. Round 3 shows strong convergence toward 5 single +5 FMO =10 as non-redundant essential set for compensation and sort gate placement, with 6 as absolute compensation floor and 11 as conservative reporting number if unstained is counted separately. AF750 FMO redundancy argument from earlier round is now largely dropped; current round treats 5 FMOs as standard.

Evidence preserved: single-stain per channel is non-negotiable; FMOs provide spillover-context negative boundaries; unstained bead data is a subset of negative tail seen in each FMO; bead-based compensation set is 6; cell-based gating set adds 5 FMOs + optionally unstained cells.

Current working understanding: 6 tubes = absolute compensation minimum. 10 tubes = 5 single-stain beads +5 FMOs = non-redundant practical essential for compensation matrix generation and sort gate placement. 11 tubes = 1 unstained/beads-only +5 singles +5 FMOs = conservative sorting-ready reporting set.

3.text:
For a streptavidin-capture 5-colour sort on AF350 / GFP / PE / AF647 / AF750 the controls that are actually used to build the matrix and to place purity-driven sort gates are bead matrix based.

Compensation is non-negotiable and bead based:
* Streptavidin beads + biotin-AF350
* Streptavidin beads + biotin-GFP
* Streptavidin beads + biotin-PE
* Streptavidin beads + biotin-AF647
* Streptavidin beads + biotin-AF750

5 single-stain streptavidin bead controls define the 5 × 5 spillover matrix. With an explicit beads-only/unstained bead reference for autofluorescence/scatter/voltage set up that is the absolute instrument/compensation minimum 1 unstained + 5 singles = 6 bead tubes.

Sort gate placement is not made against an isolated beads-only negative. On a purity-driven sorter the positive/negative boundary for each detector is set on compensated data in the presence of spillover from the other four reporters in the exact staining context that will be sorted. That is the FMO on the same bead/staining matrix:

* FMO minus AF350
* FMO minus GFP
* FMO minus PE
* FMO minus AF647
* FMO minus AF750

5 FMOs. Each FMO is the full 5-plex streptavidin bead staining minus one reporter, so the signal seen in the omitted detector is bead autofluorescence + spillover from the four reporters that are present = the operational negative used to position the sort boundary for that channel.

The beads-only/unstained streptavidin tube is useful for initial voltage/threshold checks and for documenting bead autofluorescence. Operationally that baseline is sampled inside the FMO series: every FMO contains the bead matrix and the four fluorochromes present, and the negative peak in the omitted detector is the effective negative used for gate placement. The bead autofluorescence component is also already present in the single-stain set.

Hence the non-redundant independent set that actually drives both matrix generation and compensated sort gate placement is:

5 single-stain streptavidin bead compensation controls + 5 FMO gate-setting controls = 10 essential, non-redundant controls.

That is the 5+5 operational core that is run and relied on for a sorting-ready AF350/GFP/PE/AF647/AF750 panel. The 1 unstained/beads-only + 5 single-stain = 6 tube set is the absolute compensation/negative minimum, and 1 beads-only + 5 single-stain + 5 FMO = 11 tubes is the conservative reporting-ready listing with the unstained bead baseline kept explicit for documentation/voltage set up.
